# Held: the stale frames and how to recapture them

**Status: HELD. Not regenerated by this build** (the brief's direction). The user decides each regenerated image before the release goes out (CLAUDE.md memory: never ship stale screenshots; a new frame is shown per device).

**Regenerated in scratch by the Deployer, 2026-11-13, and held in `held/frames/`** (before and after for each of the four, the three new raws and the website raw under `frames/raw/`, checksums in `frames/SHA256SUMS.txt`). Nothing was written to `website/assets/shots/` or `appstore/screenshots/` in the checkout. Three departures from the commands below, all in the scratch copy only: the website frame was captured by the `capture.mjs` Hotspot Reports job alone (the same viewport, scale, settle, clip, routes and prep, with every other job left out, so the live Weather lookup never ran) and processed by `process-img.mjs`'s one hotspot row; the backend ran with no key and with its outbound HTTP pointed at a closed local port, so the taxonomy refresh could not reach eBird and the bundled snapshot answered `/taxonomy/codes`; and the demo data was regenerated by `gen-demo-data.mjs` (the checkout's gitignored `demo-data/ebird-backup.csv` is from 2026-11-10, before 1.0.71's weather blocks, and differs). Composing all three families left frames 01 to 06 byte-identical to the committed ones; only the three `07-hotspot-reports.png` frames changed. To apply on the user's yes, copy the four `*.after.*` files and the three raws to their published paths (`deployment.md` lists them).

**Applied 2026-11-13 on the user's yes (D-15: App Store frame 7 "Keep it and update it"; website "Frame yes").** The four frames and the three raws are at their published paths, and `pipeline/app-store-listing-polish/asc/composed-frames-checksums.{json,txt}` carry the three new frames' md5, sha256 and size. The image copies were then moved out of `held/frames/` (they duplicate the published files, and the before images are in git at `2253d047`); `frames/SHA256SUMS.txt` keeps every hash. The website alt text is not changed yet: the user asked for a shorter one, and the frame and its alt reach the website in the same push.

## Which frames are stale, and why

Every frame captured from the top of a Hotspot Reports report now shows the At a glance card where the life list used to start. No other frame changes: the navigation, the tab's position and every other tab are untouched.

| Frame | Captured by | Stale because |
|---|---|---|
| `website/assets/shots/hotspot-reports.webp` | `capture.mjs`, `hotspot-reports-light.png`, then `process-img.mjs` | Shows the life list under the header; its alt text (`website-alt-text.md`) changes with it |
| `appstore/screenshots/iphone-6.9/07-hotspot-reports.png` | `capture-appstore.mjs` shot `07-hotspot-reports.png`, then `compose-appstore.mjs` | Same; the phone frame now opens on At a glance |
| `appstore/screenshots/ipad-13/07-hotspot-reports.png` | same | Same |
| `appstore/screenshots/iphone-duo/07-hotspot-reports.png` | same | Same |

The App Store caption for frame 7 ("Your own record at any one place", `appstore/LISTING.md`) stays true and is not proposed for change.

## Capture commands

From `website/tools/`, with the demo dataset and never the real data. The demo dataset's saved map style is absolute for `http://127.0.0.1:1620`, so the backend runs on 1620 (testing.md v1.0.49): stop anything else on that port first, and point `SR_DATA_DIR` at a scratch copy so the run writes nothing into the committed `demo-data/`.

```
cd website/tools
node gen-demo-data.mjs
DEMO="$(mktemp -d)" && cp -R demo-data/. "$DEMO"/
(cd ../../frontend && npm run build)
(cd ../../backend && SR_DATA_DIR="$DEMO" .venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 1620) &
# Website: the script captures every website frame; keep only hotspot-reports-light.png's result.
BASE=http://127.0.0.1:1620 node capture.mjs
node process-img.mjs          # writes ../assets/shots/*.webp; restore every webp except hotspot-reports.webp
# App Store: frame 7 only, all three families.
BASE=http://127.0.0.1:1620 SHOT=07 node capture-appstore.mjs
node compose-appstore.mjs     # writes ../../appstore/screenshots/{iphone-6.9,ipad-13,iphone-duo}/*.png
kill %1
```

`capture.mjs` has no single-shot filter, so it rewrites every website frame; only `hotspot-reports.webp` should change, and each other regenerated `.webp` is compared against the committed one and restored (`git checkout -- website/assets/shots/<file>` for any frame that differs only by capture variance) before anything is committed, per the per-image rule in `.claude/rules/docs-and-website.md` (v1.0.63). `compose-appstore.mjs` composes every family whose raw frames are present; only the three `07-hotspot-reports.png` files should differ. Magnify a crop of each new frame and compare it against the old one before showing it (the 14px favicon slots are the detail most often lost).
